questions.stem: Suppose your university is conducting a survey to collect students' opinions on the appropriate use of AI technology in assisting learning. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
In my view, AI technology, when used appropriately, is a valuable ally in learning rather than a shortcut that replaces genuine effort. Since our university is surveying students on this issue, I would like to voice my support for embracing AI in a sensible, balanced way.

There are solid reasons for this position. First, AI tools raise learning efficiency: a chatbot can explain a confusing grammar point instantly, check my essay for mistakes, or gather background material that once took hours in the library. Second, AI offers personalized tutoring, adjusting its explanations to my own pace and weak spots. Admittedly, however, over-reliance is a real danger; if students let AI think for them, their own analytical skills will gradually wither.

Therefore, the key lies in "appropriate" use. We should treat AI as an assistant that guides and inspires, not a machine that hands us ready-made answers. Used within this boundary, AI can truly make learning smarter.

sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: 1 A Florida teenager and an Atlanta woman won the overall men's and women's divisions Saturday at the annual 7 Mile Bridge Run.
Vaclav Bursa, 15, of Big Pine Key, Florida, finished first overall.
He completed the race in 41 minutes and 1 second and claimed the top spot in the men's division.
Bursa won third place in the 2022 race.
He is a student at Marathon High School.
Joanna Stephens, 28, of Atlanta, completed the course in 41 minutes and 12 seconds.
She won the women's division title and placed second overall.
The race drew competitors from 41 US states.
There were also runners from other countries, including Canada, the UK and Switzerland.
The run closed the span between the Middle and Lower Keys to traffic for 3 hours Saturday.
The April contest is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern United States.
The race field filled within minutes after online registration opened in January.

questions.stem: What does the news report say about Vaclav Bursa and Joanna Stephens?

options.text: They are young teenagers from Atlanta.
They won this year's 7 Mile Bridge Run.
They completed the race in less than 40 minutes.
They are both students at Marathon High School.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Vaclav Bursa, 15, of Big Pine Key, Florida, finished first overall.... Joanna Stephens, 28, of Atlanta, completed the course in 41 minutes and 12 seconds. She won the women's division title and placed second overall.信号：两人各自的名次陈述 。答案句不靠转折词，而靠「人物+成绩」的并列陈述定位：finished first overall 和 won the women's division title 分别说明两人都拿了各自组别第一…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：选项盗了原文真实出现的地名「Atlanta」诱你听到就选，但 Atlanta 只属于 28 岁的 Stephens；15 岁的 Bursa 来自 Florida。说两人「都是来自亚特兰大的青少年」既错配了城市，又把 28 岁的人也算成 teenager，双重不符。 借用原文：41 minutes and 1 second
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：原文用时是 41 minutes and 1 second 与 41 minutes and 12 seconds，都是 41 分多，明明大于 40 分钟；选项偏说「less than 40 minutes（少于 40 分钟）」。它盗用了「分钟数」这个耳熟数字，却把实际 41 多分钟篡改成「不到 40 分」，方向正好相反。 借用原文：He is a student at Marathon High School
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：「Marathon High School」原文确实出现，极易让人听到就选；但原文只说 He is a student at Marathon High School，这个「He」指 Bursa 一人。选项说两人「都是（both）」该校学生，把只属于 Bursa 的身份硬扣给了 Stephens。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（finished first overall ↔ won this year's 7 Mile Bridge Run 「总排名第一」=「赢了这场比赛」）

questions.evidenceText: Vaclav Bursa, 15, of Big Pine Key, Florida, finished first overall.... Joanna Stephens, 28, of Atlanta, completed the course in 41 minutes and 12 seconds. She won the women's division title and placed second overall.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the April contest?

options.text: It drew competitors from more than 40 countries.
It is watched live online by fans all over the world.
It closed the city of Big Pine Key to traffic for three hours.
It is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern U.S.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The April contest is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern United States.信号：最高级定性句即结论 。答案句靠最高级信号锁定：one of the most popular running events in the southeastern United States 是对赛事地位的定性总结，…

optionAnalysis.A: 偷换概念：原文说 drew competitors from 41 US states——来自 41 个「州」，另有 Canada, the UK and Switzerland 等少数几国选手。选项盗用「40 多」这个数量级，却把「states（州）」偷换成「countries（国家）」，参赛国其实只有零星几个，远到不了 40 个。 借用原文：after online registration opened in January
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：原文涉及「online」的只有 online registration opened in January——指线上「报名」，全文从未说有人「在线观看直播（watched live online）」。选项把「线上报名」悄悄换成「全球粉丝线上观看」，是没有原文支撑的编造。 借用原文：The run closed the span between the Middle and Lower Keys to traffic for 3 hours
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：原文是 closed the span between the Middle and Lower Keys to traffic for 3 hours——封的是中、下礁岛之间的那段「桥/路」三小时；选项把「3 hours」和「closed」原样搬来，却说封的是「the city of Big Pine Key（整座大派恩礁城）」，封闭对象被偷换了。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（one of the most popular running events in the southeastern United States ↔ It is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern U.S. 几乎逐字对应，仅缩写化）

questions.evidenceText: The April contest is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern United States.

transcript.text: 1 British astronaut Tim Peake is stepping down permanently from his role as a European astronaut.
He's going to take up a full-time position as ambassador for science and space instead—work he's been doing since 2019.
The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot was selected as a European Space Agency astronaut in 2009.
He flew to the space station for a 6-month tour in 2015.
The tour saw him control a robot on earth remotely from orbit.
He also helped dock two spacecraft.
Tim said, "Being an astronaut has been the most extraordinary experience.
I've had the privilege of working with an exceptional team of individuals during the past 13 years with the agency.
It has been incredibly exciting and rewarding.
By assuming the role of an ambassador for human flights to space, I'll continue to support the European and the UK space agencies."

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about Tim Peake?

options.text: He was once a full-time ambassador.
He was soon to retire from the army.
He used to be a helicopter pilot.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot was selected as a European Space Agency astronaut in 2009.信号：former 点出'过去身份' 。答案句开头的 The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot 里 former(过去的)就是信号词：它直接交代了 Tim Pea…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音确实念到 ambassador，但说的是他将去 take up a full-time position as ambassador——这是接下来要担任的新职，不是过去就当过；A 把'即将担任'说成 was once(曾经是),时间方向错了。 借用原文：Tim Peake is stepping down permanently from his role as a European astronaut
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：录音说的是他从'欧洲宇航员'岗位上 stepping down permanently from his role as a European astronaut(永久卸任宇航员角色)，并非从军队退役；B 把'卸任宇航员'偷换成'即将从军队退役'，army 一词也只在他过去身份里出现，并未说他要退役。 借用原文：He flew to the space station for a 6-month tour in 2015.
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：录音里 2015 对应的是 He flew to the space station for a 6-month tour in 2015.(2015 年飞往空间站)，而'被选为宇航员'是 selected as a European Space Agency astronaut in 2009(2009 年)；C 把 astronaut 与 2015 错配，年份张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot ↔ He used to be a helicopter pilot. former 名词 = used to be 动词）

questions.evidenceText: The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot was selected as a European Space Agency astronaut in 2009.

questions.stem: What does Tim Peake say about his work with the European Space Agency?

options.text: It has been unbelievably exciting and rewarding.
It has been extraordinarily tough and demanding.
It has contributed a great deal to human flights to space.
It has given him exceptional privilege as an ambassador.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P1）：It has been incredibly exciting and rewarding.信号：引语里的评价形容词即落点 。态度题的落点在当事人自述的评价词。录音引语里 It has been incredibly exciting and rewarding. 用 exciting、rewarding 两个褒…

optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：extraordinarily tough and demanding 是负面评价，但他原话是 incredibly exciting and rewarding(激动、有收获)这类褒义；B 把好评偷换成差评，极性正相反。录音里确有 extraordinary 一词(说 the most extraordinary experience)，B 借这个原词制造迷惑。 借用原文：By assuming the role of an ambassador for human flights to space
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音确有 an ambassador for human flights to space 这串词，但那是讲他将担任的新角色，不是评价这份工作'对航天贡献巨大'；题干问他怎么评价工作，C 答成'贡献'，是听到原词就选的答非所问。 借用原文：I've had the privilege of working with an exceptional team of individuals
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：录音里 privilege 出现在 I've had the privilege of working with an exceptional team(有幸与优秀团队共事)，讲的是与团队合作的荣幸，不是'作为 ambassador 的特殊荣誉'；D 把 privilege 和 ambassador 硬凑到一起，张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（incredibly exciting and rewarding ↔ unbelievably exciting and rewarding incredibly = unbelievably 同义替换）

questions.evidenceText: It has been incredibly exciting and rewarding.

transcript.text: 1 An Asda store in Wales is now home to five cats after they wandered in and made themselves comfortable.
The supermarket is known for its loyal customers, but now has a different kind of visitor that has appeared over the last year.
Regular shoppers at the supermarket are familiar with the sight of several cats settling down in the shop aisles.
The unusual situation started about 12 months ago, when one cat routinely started visiting the store.
Local newspapers reported that puzzled customers posted on Facebook groups to try to find out if the cat was lost.
But its owner assured the concerned customers it was very much loved and fed at home.
It just enjoyed visiting the shop.
Staff did their best to discourage the pet from hanging around.
But instead of leaving and never coming back, it invited its friends round.
There are now at least five different cats who come almost on a daily basis.
They visit the store so much that staff have been forced to put up signs, asking their customers not to feed them.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the five cats seen in the Asda store?

options.text: They are known for their loyalty to their owners.
They are brought in by the store's customers.
They are regular visitors to the store.
They are pets kept by the store staff.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Regular shoppers at the supermarket are familiar with the sight of several cats settling down in the shop aisles. There are now at least five different cats who come almost on a daily basis.信号：客观陈述句直接交代猫的常态 。新闻里没有转折，答案就藏在平铺直叙交代事实的句子里：several cats settling down in the shop aisles 配上 five different cat…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：loyalty to their owners 抓住了录音里的 loyal 这个原词，可录音 The supermarket is known for its loyal customers 说的是超市以"忠实顾客"闻名，忠诚指的是人、不是猫，更没说猫忠于主人。听到 loyal 就选 A，正中原词陷阱。 借用原文：wandered in and made themselves comfortable
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：brought in by the store's customers 听起来合理，但录音明说猫是 wandered in and made themselves comfortable（自己晃进来安顿下来），第一只是 one cat routinely started visiting the store，没有任何"顾客带进来"的内容，属凭常识硬安、原文未提及。 借用原文：Staff did their best to discourage the pet from hanging around
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：pets kept by the store staff 借了录音里的 staff 和 pet 两个原词，可录音里 Staff did their best to discourage the pet from hanging around 说的是店员想方设法"赶"猫、不让它逗留，恰恰说明猫不归店员所有。听到 staff、pet 就选 D，又是原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（five different cats who come almost on a daily basis ↔ regular visitors to the store "几乎每天来"="常客"）

questions.evidenceText: Regular shoppers at the supermarket are familiar with the sight of several cats settling down in the shop aisles. There are now at least five different cats who come almost on a daily basis.

questions.stem: What did some customers think when they saw the first cat routinely appear in the store?

options.text: It might be a nuisance to the loyal shoppers.
It might have been abandoned by its owner.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Local newspapers reported that puzzled customers posted on Facebook groups to try to find out if the cat was lost.信号：顾客行为句直接道出"以为它丢了" 。描述顾客当时反应的句子就是答案句：puzzled customers posted on Facebook groups to try to find out if the cat…

optionAnalysis.A: 答非所问：nuisance to the loyal shoppers 借了 loyal/shoppers 的影子，但录音里顾客看到第一只猫时是 puzzled（困惑），去打听它是否走丢，并没有觉得它"惹人嫌"。猫多到要贴告示是后文的事，且也没说它惹忠实顾客嫌，时间和内容都对不上。 借用原文：if the cat was lost
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：abandoned by its owner 与正解贴得最近，都是"它出事了"，但录音里顾客打听的是 if the cat was lost（是否走丢），是"丢"不是"主人不要了"。况且下文 its owner assured the concerned customers it was very much loved 说主人很爱它，根本没被遗弃。错在偷换了"走丢"与"被弃"这两个相近却不同的概念。 借用原文：The unusual situation started about 12 months ago
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：It might be 12 months old. 抓住录音真念过的 12 个月，但录音 The unusual situation started about 12 months ago 说的是"这桩怪事大约始于 12 个月前"，12 个月是"猫开始来店多久"，根本不是"猫 12 个月大"。听到 12 months 就选 C，是典型的数字原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（to try to find out if the cat was lost ↔ It might have got lost. "想弄清是否走丢"="它可能走丢了"）

questions.evidenceText: Local newspapers reported that puzzled customers posted on Facebook groups to try to find out if the cat was lost.

questions.stem: What are customers asked not to do?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：They visit the store so much that staff have been forced to put up signs, asking their customers not to feed them.信号：请求句 asking…not to 直接给出禁止内容 。答案句末尾的请求结构就是定位信号：asking their customers not to feed them（要求顾客不要喂它们）。听到 not to + …

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：Remove any store signs. 抓住录音真念过的 signs，可录音 staff have been forced to put up signs 说的是店员"贴"告示，从没要求顾客"撤"告示。听到 signs 就选 B，正中原词陷阱，且把"贴"反成了"撤"。 借用原文：several cats settling down in the shop aisles
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：Sit in the shop aisles. 借了录音原词 aisles，可录音 several cats settling down in the shop aisles 说的是猫在过道里安顿，不是顾客坐过道，更没人要求顾客别坐。听到 aisles 就选 C，是原词陷阱加张冠李戴。 借用原文：asking their customers not to feed them
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：Bring in pets with them. 蹭了录音里的 pet 一词，但录音里店员唯一对顾客提的要求是 not to feed them（别喂猫），从没说过"别带宠物进店"。带宠物进店是凭常识联想出来的，原文并未提及。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（not to feed them ↔ Feed the cats. "不要喂它们"对应被禁动作"喂猫"）

questions.evidenceText: They visit the store so much that staff have been forced to put up signs, asking their customers not to feed them.

transcript.text: W: I've been thinking about moving off campus next semester.
transcript.zh: W: 我一直在考虑下学期搬出学校住。

transcript.text: M: Hmm… I don't know if that's a good idea as your mother and I would worry about you living all by yourself in an apartment so far from home. And then there's the expense, too. I'm not sure we can afford it.
transcript.zh: M: 嗯……我不知道这是不是个好主意，你妈妈和我会担心你一个人住在离家这么远的公寓里。还有费用问题。我不确定我们负担得起。

transcript.text: W: Well, I wouldn't be alone, actually. Three of my friends from the dormitory would share the place with me. And with four of us, it wouldn't cost any more than living in the dorm.
transcript.zh: W: 其实我不会一个人住。宿舍里的三个朋友会和我一起合租。我们四个人的话，花费不会比住宿舍多。

transcript.text: M: Are you sure about that? Rents in big cities are high, and then there's the cost of electricity and gas. Have you factored those in?
transcript.zh: M: 你确定吗?大城市的房租很高，还有电费和燃气费。你把这些都算进去了吗?

transcript.text: W: We've budgeted for those, and for Internet and transportation. And if we move far enough from the city center, the rent is low enough for us to afford all of it.
transcript.zh: W: 我们已经把这些都做了预算，还有网费和交通费。如果我们搬得离市中心远一点，房租就足够低,我们能负担得起所有这些。

transcript.text: M: What's about the commute to and from campus? It sounds like you'll be wasting several hours every day on the road instead of studying.
transcript.zh: M: 那往返学校怎么办?听起来你每天要在路上浪费好几个小时，而不是用来学习。

transcript.text: W: It's about an hour to campus, but there's no reason I can't study on the bus. After all, I did that during high school and my commute was even longer then.
transcript.zh: W: 到学校大约一小时，但我完全可以在公交车上学习。毕竟我高中时就是这么做的，那时候通勤时间还更长呢。

transcript.text: M: That's true. But I'm not sure why you want to leave campus and go through all that trouble when the cost is the same.
transcript.zh: M: 这倒是真的。但我不明白既然费用一样，你为什么要离开学校，费这么大劲儿。

transcript.text: W: For a lot of reasons. We'd have a kitchen, so we could cook ourselves. And we'd each have our own bedroom, where we could study instead of going to the library. We just have more space and privacy.
transcript.zh: W: 原因有很多。我们会有厨房，可以自己做饭。而且我们每个人都有自己的卧室，可以在那里学习，不用去图书馆。我们就是有更多空间和隐私。

transcript.text: M: I'm not convinced that the benefits are greater than the disadvantages, but I'll discuss this with your mother.
transcript.zh: M: 我还不确定好处是否大于坏处，但我会和你妈妈商量一下。

questions.stem: What has the woman been thinking of doing next semester?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：W: I've been thinking about moving off campus next semester.信号：开场首句直陈打算 。信号是女方对话开场第一句的直接陈述 I've been thinking about moving off campus next semester.，与题干 thinking of doing …

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：Sharing her room with friends. 借了后文女方说的 Three of my friends from the dormitory would share the place with me，但那是『四人合租整套房子』，不是『与朋友合住一个房间』，且非她最初的打算，是把后文细节错安到本题。 借用原文：And then there's the expense, too.
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：Cutting down her living expenses. 盗用了原文反复出现的 the expense 一词，但女方的打算是搬出校外，省钱只是搬出后讨论的一个方面，不是她『在考虑做的事』本身，听到 expense 就选会落坑。 借用原文：if we move far enough from the city center
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：Moving to the city center. 与原文正相反：女方说的是 if we move far enough from the city center（搬到离市中心足够远的地方），选项却说搬向市中心，极性反了。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（moving off campus ↔ Living off campus moving=living 同指搬离校园住）

questions.evidenceText: W: I've been thinking about moving off campus next semester.

questions.stem: What does the man suggest the woman take into consideration?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：M: Are you sure about that? Rents in big cities are high, and then there's the cost of electricity and gas. Have you factored those in?信号：连列费用项+反问提醒 。信号是男方一口气列出 Rents in big cities are high, and then there's the cost of electricity and gas 并反问 Ha…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：The facilities available. 看似贴居住话题，但原文男方提醒的是费用，厨房、卧室等设施是后文女方自己列搬出去的好处 We'd have a kitchen，并非男方让她『考虑』的事，张冠李戴。 借用原文：if we move far enough from the city center, the rent is low enough
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：Changes in living conditions. 借用了贯穿全程的 living 一词，但男方让考虑的是『费用』这一具体方面，不是笼统的『生活条件变化』，把具体范畴偷换成宽泛说法。 借用原文：living all by yourself in an apartment so far from home
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：The distance to her home. 盗用了男方开头 so far from home 里的 home 一词，但那是男方表达担忧的话，并非他要女方『纳入考虑』的方面，且真正反复提醒的是费用，听到 home 就选会落坑。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Rents in big cities are high, and then there's the cost of electricity and gas ↔ Various costs involved 罗列各项费用=概括为各种费用）

questions.evidenceText: M: Are you sure about that? Rents in big cities are high, and then there's the cost of electricity and gas. Have you factored those in?

transcript.text: M: Of course you did. Everyone did. And kids enjoy it just as much today as you and I did when we were young. Some games just never get old.

transcript.text: 1 We assume that if we offer our customers more choices, then they'll be more likely to buy our products.
But here's the paradox of choice: if a person is presented with too many choices, they are actually less likely to buy.
In 2012, psychologists published a study about jams.
On a regular day at a local food market, people would find a display table with 24 different kinds of jams.
Then on another day, at that same food market, people were given only 6 different types of jam choices.

Guess which display table led to more sales? 2 The study found that while the bigger display table created more interest, people were almost 10 times less likely to purchase a jar of jam than in the case of the smaller display.
Customer satisfaction takes a hit as well.
In the study, the bigger display of jams leads to lower customer satisfaction than the smaller display.
In an extensive study published in 2015, researchers analyzed a total of 99 choice studies and specifically looked at those cases in which reducing choices helped to boost sales.

They found four rules that motivate consumers to buy: when people want to make a quick and easy choice, when the product is complex, when it's difficult to compare alternatives, and when consumers don't have clear preferences.
So as you can see, when it comes to choices, less is more.

transcript.text: 1 The New Year has come and gone, and many may have already forgotten what they had resolved to do on January 1st.
But if that resolution was to volunteer more, now is the best time to start.
Volunteering can drop after the holiday season, and by February, some organizations lack the volunteers they had in surplus just a month ago.
According to one survey, only 26% of Americans volunteered, despite reports that many Americans view volunteering as worthwhile. 2 Why such a disconnect?
Most people cite time and conflicting work schedules as major barriers, but employees and employers would actually benefit if companies made employee volunteering part of the job.
Researchers have found donating our time and talent to others can lower blood pressure, boost happiness and improve mental and physical health.
Studies have also linked employee volunteer programs with more productive employees.
With so much emphasis on employee wellness these days, company volunteer programs could be the perfect 2025 resolution.
But for volunteering to benefit employees and the workplace, the entire organization needs to be involved.
By allowing employees to donate their time during work hours, the workplace becomes an outlet for personal fulfillment without affecting personal time.
In one survey, 89% of employees perceived companies that sponsored volunteer activities as creating a better working environment, and 75% said volunteering was critical to their well-being.

Everything from specialist cheeses to sought-after coffee beans gets thrown away every day in the current food system. 2 This is where French entrepreneur Sophie André comes in.
In 2016 she moved to London and began by setting up a business delivering luxury hand-made food across the city.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Freshly juiced fruit has become a basic dietary item—especially for busy, health-conscious consumers who can save time on making (and perhaps even chewing) their food without missing out on nutrients. Fruit juice also has been linked to claims that it can help you both lose weight and stay healthy. All of which, of course, has made it highly profitable. The global fruit and vegetable juices market was valued at $154 billion in 2016 and is expected to grow.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: But is juicing really as healthy as we think? Most foods containing fructose—a naturally occurring sugar found in all fruits and fruit juices—don't seem to have harmful effects as long as they're not contributing to excess daily calories. This is because the fibre found in whole fruits is intact, and the sugar is contained within the fruit's cells. It takes our digestive system a while to break these cells down and for fructose to enter the bloodstream.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: But this is not the case with fruit juice. Unlike whole fruit, fruit juice has most of the fibre removed. This is why the fructose in fruit juices counts as 'free sugars'—which also include honey and the sugars added to foods. It's recommended by the World Health Organisation that adults have no more than 30g of added sugar, the equivalent of 150ml of fruit juice, per day. The problem is that, with the fibre removed, fruit juice's fructose is absorbed more quickly. Sudden increases in blood sugar cause the release of insulin(胰岛素) to bring it back down to a stable level. Over time, this mechanism can wear out, increasing the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. In 2013, researchers analysed the health data of 100,000 people collected between 1986 and 2009 and found that fruit juice consumption was linked with increased risk of type 2 diabetes. Another study found a relationship between fruit juice and type 2 diabetes after following the diets and diabetes status of more than 70,000 nurses over 18 years. The researchers explain that the possible reason for this may partly have been the lack of the other components found in whole fruit, like fibre.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Juices containing vegetables can provide more nutrients and less sugar than juices made up of just fruit—but they still lack valuable fibre. Diets high in fibre have been linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure and diabetes, and it's recommended adults consume 30g per day.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Aside from the link to type 2 diabetes, many studies agree that fruit juice is harmful if it contributes to an excess in calories. In an analysis of 155 studies, John Sievenpiper, associate professor at the University of Toronto's Department of Nutritional Sciences, set out to understand if the associations between sugary soft drinks and health—including risk of diabetes and heart disease—were applicable to the food and drink we generally consume as part of a healthy diet. He compared studies looking into the effects of fructose-containing sugars with control diets free from or lower in these sugars. His aim? To isolate the effects of consuming too many calories from the effects of foods containing different sugars.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: He found negative effects on blood sugar and insulin levels when food provided excess calories from sugars, including fruit juice. However, when the calories weren't in excess overall, there were some advantages to consuming whole fruit—and even fruit juice. Sievenpiper concludes that the recommended 150ml of fruit juice per day, which is an average serving, is reasonable. The paper concluded that foods containing fructose may have some small benefits for long-term blood sugar control when they don't lead to over-consumption of calories. But when they do lead to too many calories, they risk raising blood sugar and insulin levels.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: So while we know that fruit juice can cause diabetes if it's part of a diet that has more calories overall, it's less clear how juice affects the long-term health of those who aren't overweight. But we have a higher risk of consuming more than the recommended daily number of calories (around 2,000 for women and 2,500 for men) on the days we drink juice, according to research. Numerous studies have shown that drinking fruit juice doesn't make us consume any less of other foods throughout the day.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: As it is easy to consume large amounts of fruit juice quite quickly, extra calories are taken in. And extra calories can contribute to weight gain. One way we can improve the effects of fruit juice on our health is making sure we select ripe fruit to retain as much of its goodness as possible, according to Roger Clemens, professor of pharmaceutical(药物的) sciences at the University of Southern California.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Another reason for fruit juice's recent popularity is the argument that it can help to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body. However, "the whole concept of a juice diet helping to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body is completely false," says Clemens. "We consume compounds every day that may be poisonous and our bodies do a wonderful job of removing and eliminating anything harmful from our bodies."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: And juice isn't a cure-all for getting your nutrients, either. "There are a lot of nutrients contained in the parts of the fruits, such as in apple skins, that are excluded when you juice them," says Heather Ferris, a professor of medicine. "You end up with sugary water with some vitamins."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Plus, she adds, it's not an ideal way to reach the advised 'five a day'. "People try to get five servings of fruit and vegetables per day and don't realise this isn't just about getting vitamins," she says. "It's also about reducing the amount of grain carbs(碳水化合物) and protein and fats in our diet, and increasing fibre." So while fruit juice is better than no fruit at all, there are limits. It particularly comes with risks when we consume more than 150ml of free sugars per day, or when it puts us over our recommended calorie intake. It provides us with vitamins—but fruit juice is far from a quick fix.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. Granted, you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The most major indicator of classical music's importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works. Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic(交响乐的) orchestras have had on society's taste in music.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. Some of the world's greatest hits have been parts of rock operas.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.
